text:
Here are two ideas to get you started (but you can write any kind of poem you like):

Idea 1

Write a limerick, like the ones you read in Activity 2.
  1. Have another read of the examples in Activity 2 to get the rhythm in your head.
  2. Think about the rhyming word at the end of the first line to get you started. That should be your first line sorted, starting with “There was a” and ending with your rhyming word.
  3. Try saying the words out loud until you have a poem that you’re happy with, then write it down so you don’t forget it!


Idea 2

Talk with your pen. This sounds like a funny idea, but it’s the kind of thing Michael Rosen does in lots of his poems, including ‘Strict’ in Activity 1. Talking with your pen is where you just write down some thoughts or ideas, maybe about something you’ve seen or heard.
  1. Imagine that you’re telling someone about it, but instead of saying the words, write them down.
  2. Michael Rosen turns these ideas into poems partly through the way he repeats lines. See if you can include some repetition to turn your thoughts into a poem.
Have a go at inventing your own poem and then performing it, either to someone at home, over the phone or by filming yourself.
